beliefs: With all controls at minimum and switch off, the dot is at (0,0) with size 1.0 [E1]
Switch on with all dials at minimum moves the dot to y=10, leaving x and size unchanged [E2]
Dial a moves the dot in x and increases size: x=2a and size=1+0.5a [E3]
Dial b moves the dot in x negatively: x=-b, size unchanged [E4]
Dial c moves the dot in y and increases size: y=c and size=1+0.5c [E5]

The switch adds 10 to y when c=0 [E2], but when c>0 the switch adds only (10-c) to y, i.e. y = c + max(0, 10-c) = max(c,10)... but E7 shows y=7 for c=3, so switch adds (10-c) only partially? Actually y=7 = c + (10-c)*? — unresolved [E6, E7]

E7: c=3, switch on gives y=7, not 10 and not 3; E6: c=5, switch on gives y=5. So switch contribution decreases with c: y = c + (10-c) when c<5? c=3→7, c=5→5, c=0→10. This fits y = c + (10-c) = 10 for c<5? No: c=3→10 not 7. Try y = c + (10-c)/? — c=3→7 means added 4; c=5→5 means added 0; c=0→10 means added 10. Added = 10 - 2c? c=3→4, c=5→0, c=0→10. Yes! y = c + (10-2c) = 10 - c for c≤5, and y=c for c≥5 [E2,E6,E7]
So switch on: y = 10 - c if c<5, else y = c (i.e. y = max(c, 10-c) with crossover at c=5) [E2,E6,E7]
How a and c combine on size (additive vs max) is still unknown? [E3,E5]
notes: E7 (c=3,switch on → y=7) plus E6 (c=5→y=5) and E2 (c=0→y=10) fit y = 10 - c for c≤5 and y = c for c≥5, i.e. switch on gives y = max(c, 10-c). Replaced the max(c,10) rule.
